source_facts: ProviderService persists activeTurnId in ProviderSessionDirectory runtimePayload when a turn starts, but recovery currently reads cwd/model/resume cursor rather than the active turn.
OpenCode session.status is activity evidence only; idle does not encode terminal outcome and a missing status-map entry is also treated as idle.
OpenCode promptAsync accepts a caller-supplied messageID and assistant messages retain the corresponding user message in parentID.
T3 exact turn completion is guarded against settling a different newer active turn, while generic session.state.changed ready clears the session-wide active turn.
OpenCode abort waits for runner cancellation and its idle callback before returning, so abort response and idle SSE delivery can race.
The OpenCode adapter currently accepts an explicit interrupt turn id without checking it against the adapter-local active turn.
The OpenCode adapter currently maps any idle event to completed when an active turn id exists, even when no turn-specific provider evidence accompanies the idle event.
OpenCode readThread and rollbackThread currently call session.messages without a limit, cursor, timeout, or abort budget.
ProviderSessionReaper reads a projected activeTurnId and later calls stopSession using only the thread id, leaving a check-then-stop window.
ProviderService and the OpenCode adapter use unbounded runtime-event queues, so stalled consumers remain a separate pressure and ordering risk.

historical_precedent.lesson: Mid-turn steering has produced a permanently working thread whose disabled input survives restart.
Repeated mid-run comments have left T3 working after the underlying OpenCode session ended.
Losing durable provider-session identity silently split one visible T3 thread across multiple OpenCode sessions.
The first resume repair required follow-up review fixes so transient/auth failures did not create empty sessions and resumed sessions reapplied current permissions.
Unbounded session.messages hydration can hang large threads indefinitely; recovery history inspection must be bounded and time-limited.
OpenCode child-process and SSE disconnections have historically lacked automatic reconnection and clear user-visible failure states.

repair_candidates.reason: Generic ready clears the current turn without exact provider-session or turn affinity.
Idle is activity state, not proof of completed, failed, aborted, or lost execution.
The existing full-history path has a documented large-thread hang and no timeout.

repair_candidates.summary: Persist exact T3 turn and ordered OpenCode user-message affinity, subscribe before snapshot, query status, inspect only bounded time-limited matching history, and emit one exact terminal result.
A stale reaper snapshot must not stop a session whose binding or adapter turn changed before stop commits; implementation location remains open.
